suggestions.assertion: Every KQL query in hunts.md is time-bounded (ago(), between, or Sentinel {{StartTimeISO}} placeholders)
suggestions.reason: The machine pre-grade treats every ```kql fence as a query, so a let-only IOC block (B, C) counts as 'unbounded', and its fence tracking breaks on the ```yaml block in C (it reported a block starting '--- ## 4.'). More importantly the assertion has no stated position on XDR custom-detection drafts, which legitimately omit a Timestamp filter because the platform owns the lookback: A satisfied it with ingestion_time() > ago(4h), C omitted the bound and explained why. State whether a detection draft must still carry ago()/ingestion_time() or is exempt.

The report's SHA256 is 65 hex characters (verified with wc -c), so any hash sweep built from it can never match. Only run C noticed; A and B shipped hash clauses and A even annotated it 'MDE stores hashes lower-case'. If the malformed hash is deliberate, add an assertion for noticing it; if accidental, fix the fixture, because it silently invalidates the hash IOC in every pack.

suggestions.assertion: Each query carries a MITRE ATT&CK mapping that names the behaviour (e.g. T1204.004 or T1204.002, T1059.001, T1053.005, T1071.001, T1041/T1567), not a generic placeholder
suggestions.reason: 'Each query' cannot be met literally by a vendor-alert sweep (AlertEvidence/SecurityAlert) or a preflight/coverage query; A and C mark those with a dash and a reason. Clarify that hunt queries over raw telemetry need a mapping and alert/preflight queries are exempt, otherwise graders will split on it.

eval_feedback.overall: Run C fails only assertion 8, and only on the detection-ready draft that intentionally omits a Timestamp filter; whether that should fail depends on a rule the assertion does not state. It is also the only run that caught the malformed hash.
